title: What digit z makes 31z5 a multiple of nine?
description: A missing digit is found from the digit sum rule for nine. The video shows why the digit sum can be nine or eighteen, and so why there are two answers.
teaching_notes: One idea: the digit sum of a multiple of nine is a multiple of nine, so the missing digit is found by listing the multiples of nine that the digit sum can reach. Watch for students who stop at the first digit that works and never look for the second.

video_script.why: The student knows that a number and its digit sum leave the same remainder on division by nine and now uses the digit sum to find a missing digit.
video_script.substitution: Add the known digits, write the digit sum with the missing digit, and list the multiples of nine that this sum can reach.
video_script.anchor: the number three one z five on a board, with a strip of multiples of nine below it
video_script.payoff_line: The digit z is zero or nine

final_answer.spoken: z is zero or nine, giving three thousand one hundred five or three thousand one hundred ninety five

maths_rules: a number is divisible by 9 exactly when its digit sum is divisible by 9
the digit sum of 31z5 is 3 + 1 + z + 5 = 9 + z
z is a digit from 0 to 9, so 9 + z lies from 9 to 18
the multiples of 9 from 9 to 18 are 9 and 18, so z = 0 or z = 9
the next multiple, 27, needs z = 18, which is not a digit
video_script.design: The number with a box for the missing digit, and a strip of multiples of nine. The strip shows that nine plus z can land on nine or on eighteen, which is why there are two answers.
